```{r}
##### summarising methodologies into a table #####

method_summary <- Data_complete %>%
  group_by(registry) %>%
  summarise(
    n_methods = n_distinct(project_methodologies),
    methods   = paste(sort(unique(project_methodologies)), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(registry)

method_summary

# making a table

install.packages("flextable")
install.packages("officer")

library(flextable)
library(officer)

# Build the flextable
ft <- flextable(method_summary)

# Autofit registry + count, but wrap methods column
ft <- autofit(ft) %>%
  width(j = 3, width = 4) %>%   # make the methods column 4 inches wide
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit") %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  add_header_lines("Summary of unique forest project methodologies per registry") %>%
  align(align = "left", part = "all")   # left-align wrapped text

# Save to Word
doc <- read_docx() %>%
  body_add_flextable(ft) %>%
  body_end_section_landscape()   # optional: makes it landscape if table is wide

print(doc, target = "forest_methods_by_registry_try4.docx")

###--------------------------------------------

##### Finding duplicates in methodologies #####

# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(flextable)
library(officer)

method_summary_clean <- method_summary %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # split into a list of methods per registry
    methods_vec = list(str_split(methods, ";\\s*")[[1]] %>% str_trim()),
    # remove duplicates + sort
    methods_unique = list(sort(unique(methods_vec))),
    # recombine into string
    methods = paste(methods_unique, collapse = "; "),
    # count unique
    n_methods = length(methods_unique)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(registry, n_methods, methods) %>%
  arrange(registry)

# --- make nicely wrapped table for Word ---
ft <- flextable(method_summary_clean) %>%
  autofit() %>%
  width(j = 3, width = 4) %>%   # wrap 3rd column (methods)
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit") %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%
  add_header_lines("Summary of unique forest project methodologies per registry (deduplicated)") %>%
  align(align = "left", part = "all")

ft
# --- export to Word file ---
doc <- read_docx() %>%
  body_add_flextable(ft) %>%
  body_end_section_landscape()   # optional: remove if you prefer portrait

print(doc, target = "forest_methods_by_registry_deduplicated.docx")









#### preparing data for alluvial plot #####

Data_diff <- Data_complete %>%
  filter(proponent_country_manual != host_country_or_area)

flow_matrix <- Data_diff %>%
  mutate(sum_of_credit_volume = as.numeric(sum_of_credit_volume)) %>%  # Convert to numeric
  group_by(buyer_continent, project_continent) %>%
  summarise(total_volume = sum(sum_of_credit_volume, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = project_continent,
    values_from = total_volume,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("buyer_continent")

# View the result
print(flow_matrix)

#Put it into alluvial format
# Convert the matrix to a data frame
flow_df <- as.data.frame(flow_matrix)

# Add the source column from row names
flow_df <- flow_df %>%
  mutate(source = rownames(flow_matrix)) %>%
  relocate(source)

# View the result
print(flow_df)

df_long <- flow_df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -source, names_to = "target", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(value > 0) %>%  # Optional: remove zero flows
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = unique(source)),
    target = factor(target, levels = unique(target))
  )

#Create alluvial plots for flows between regions
#Plot with labels
p <- ggplot(df_long,
       aes(axis1 = source, axis2 = target, y = value)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = source), width = 1/12) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "grey", color = "black") +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Origin", "Retirement"), expand = c(.05, .05))  +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Africa" = "#4f2fee",
    "Asia" = "#42999b",
    "Europe" = "#70ffc4",
    "North America" = "#fac723",
    "South America" = "#ff5c9a",
    "Oceania" = "#b25b68"
  )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Forest-based carbon flows between regions")

#Plot without labels
p2 <- ggplot(df_long,
       aes(axis1 = source, axis2 = target, y = value)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = source), width = 1/12) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "grey", color = "black") +
  #geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Origin", "Retirement"), expand = c(.05, .05))  +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Africa" = "#4f2fee",
    "Asia" = "#42999b",
    "Europe" = "#70ffc4",
    "North America" = "#fac723",
    "South America" = "#ff5c9a",
    "Oceania" = "#b25b68"
  )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Forest-based carbon flows between regions")

print(p2)

# Export to both plots
ggsave("/Users/zoe/Desktop/CCBP/CCBP_database/figures/alluvial_plot_text_zl_testing.png", plot = p, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("/Users/zoe/Desktop/CCBP/CCBP_database/figures/alluvial_plot_zl_testing.png", plot = p2, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

#Create the plot for flows between countries
# Make sure Credit.Volume is numeric
Data_complete <- Data_diff %>%
  mutate(Credit.Volume = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", Credit.Volume)))

# Summarise and reshape to long format for alluvial plot
df_long_country <- Data_complete %>%
  group_by(Headquarter.Country, Project.Country) %>%
  summarise(value = sum(Credit.Volume, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(source = Headquarter.Country, target = Project.Country)

# Create the alluvial plot with labels
p3 <- ggplot(df_long_country,
            aes(axis1 = source, axis2 = target, y = value)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = source), width = 1/12, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "grey90", color = "black") +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2, hjust = 0) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Origin", "Retirement"), expand = c(.05, .05)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Forest-based carbon flows between countries")

# Print the plot
print(p3)
ggsave("C:/Users/uqbwil14/Dropbox/Carbon crossing borders project/Rcode_bw/CCBP/figures/countries_text.png", plot = p3, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# Create the alluvial plot without labels
p4 <- ggplot(df_long_country,
            aes(axis1 = source, axis2 = target, y = value)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = source), width = 1/12, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "grey90", color = "black") +
  #geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2, hjust = 0) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Origin", "Retirement"), expand = c(.05, .05)) +
```

Summaries for reporting purposes
```{r}
# Make sure Credit.Volume is numeric
Data_complete <- Data_complete %>%
  mutate(Credit.Volume = as.numeric(Credit.Volume))

# Group and summarise
top_countries <- Data_complete %>%
  group_by(Headquarter.Country) %>%
  summarise(Total_Credit = sum(Credit.Volume, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Credit))

# View result
print(top_countries)

# Summarise by Project.Country
top_projects <- Data_complete %>%
  group_by(Project.Country) %>%
  summarise(Total_Credit = sum(Credit.Volume, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Credit)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)  # Top 10

# View result
print(top_projects)

## hello ##

print(top_projects)
```
